How They Handle Restricted Countries

When it comes to restricted countries, Stripe's limited global reach is a major liability. In contrast, alternative solutions like Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy often employ complex workarounds and third-party integrations to accommodate creators in restricted countries, but these solutions are often fragile and prone to failure. On the other hand, sovereign commerce infrastructure solutions like Edge Commerce Stack don't just accommodate restricted countries - they're designed from the ground up to operate in environments where conventional payment processors are unavailable or severely restricted.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, the difference between conventional payment processors and sovereign commerce infrastructure solutions is stark. Conventional payment processors like Stripe and PayPal charge high fees, often ranging from 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction to 3.5% + $0.15 per transaction, with additional fees for things like currency conversion and chargeback protection. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure solutions like Edge Commerce Stack charge a flat fee of $197 for the Edge Commerce Stack deployment, with no ongoing fees or subscriptions - and with automatic payment processing and order storage built right in.

Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

When it comes to ownership, automation, and delivery, conventional payment processors and sovereign commerce infrastructure solutions diverge sharply. Conventional payment processors like Stripe and PayPal often require creators to surrender ownership of their data and customer relationships, while sovereign commerce infrastructure solutions like Edge Commerce Stack give creators complete control over their data and customer relationships, with automatic payment processing and order storage built right in. Plus, with Edge Commerce Stack, creators can automate their entire commerce workflow, from order storage to file delivery, with a single, integrated platform.
